root_idea.summary: The root centers on one thing catching up with, reaching, or joining another.
root_idea.development: From this orientation develop meanings of overtaking and attainment, successive joining, reaching an endpoint, perception as attaining knowledge, and downward levels or depths.

senses.definition: To attain, reach, overtake, or catch up with someone or something.
senses.usage_conditions: Used for physical pursuit and for reaching a person, thing, time, or event. The Quranic occurrences include both overtaking and attaining an endpoint.

senses.definition: To perceive, comprehend, or attain knowledge of something.
senses.usage_conditions: May refer to sensory perception or to intellectual comprehension; the Quranic construction contrasts human perception with divine perception.

senses.definition: To reach an utmost limit and thereby come to an end, fail, or become exhausted.
senses.usage_conditions: Attested in Lane’s discussion of a Quranic reading concerning knowledge of the Hereafter; this is an endpoint or exhaustion sense rather than ordinary pursuit.

senses.definition: To catch up with one another, overtake one another, or arrive successively until all are joined.
senses.usage_conditions: A reciprocal or collective construction; it can describe the last of a group reaching the first or successive arrival in a place.

senses.definition: To reach someone with favor, aid, or relief; to come to someone’s rescue.
senses.usage_conditions: Used especially of a benefaction or mercy reaching a person and averting a bad outcome.

senses.definition: To run on to an endpoint or completion; of knowledge, to reach or fail to reach the matter of the Hereafter.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic expression about knowledge of the Hereafter has variant readings and interpretations, including knowledge reaching its limit, becoming clear only later, or proceeding until it is cut short.

senses.definition: Overtaking or being caught up with.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic expression, it denotes the feared pursuit or overtaking of the Israelites by Pharaoh.

senses.definition: A consequence, liability, or adverse claim that catches up with a person.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic passage is also explained as referring to an adverse consequence or liability rather than physical pursuit.

senses.definition: A bottom, lowest depth, or descending level; specifically, a stage of Hell.
senses.usage_conditions: Opposed to an ascending degree or stage; in the Quranic expression it denotes the lowest level of the Fire.

senses.definition: Overtaken, reached, or caught up with.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic occurrence is a passive participle describing people who are to be overtaken.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The dropping of rain in close succession, as though one portion overtakes another.
Hanging a rope around a person’s neck to couple that person with another.
Uninterrupted continuation or performance, with one part following another without a gap.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to successive actions such as thrusting, drinking, or striking.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The overtaking or catching up of hunted animals by a horse.
To obtain, acquire, or secure something, including revenge or retaliation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A classical extension of attaining something sought.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To reach the proper or final stage; to mature or ripen.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Said of a person reaching maturity or puberty, fruit becoming ripe, a pot reaching the proper cooking stage, or wine maturing; water may also be said to reach the bottom of a well.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a payment or price to become obligatory upon the purchaser.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic, figurative use of reaching or becoming due.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To continue or proceed uninterruptedly, with one part closely following another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a course, journey, or successive reports and other sequences.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To repair, correct, or supplement an omission or error.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of correcting a statement, supplying something omitted, or following up a neglected matter with what completes it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The attainment or acquisition of a desired object, and the seeking of that attainment.
A rope or rope-piece attached to the lower end of a well rope and connected to the bucket.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It is the portion next to the water and helps keep the main rope from rotting.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A ring or thong belonging to a bowstring, or an added piece joining a belt, rope, or cord that is too short.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The precise object varies with the construction described.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An imperative verbal noun meaning “attain,” “reach,” or “overtake.”
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A fixed imperative expression associated with the otherwise unused Form I verb دَرَكَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An animal that is hunted.
One who attains, reaches, or overtakes often or quickly; by extension, one possessing strong or rapid perception.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An epithet applied to a person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place or time at which attainment occurs; by extension, a source or means from which something is obtained.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In legal terminology, مَدَارِكُ الشَّرْعِ refers to the sources and methods by which legal rulings are reached.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Perceived by the senses or apprehended by the intellect.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: As a passive participial adjective, it can contrast sensory perception with intellectual apprehension.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The perceptive or apprehending faculty of the mind.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Usually in the technical expression القُوَّةُ المُدْرِكَةُ or its substantivized form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In plural technical usage, the five perceptive faculties or senses.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Occurs in expressions such as المُدْرِكَاتُ الخَمْسُ and المَدَارِكُ الخَمْسُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A reported anatomical term for the area between the shoulder blades where a cupping vessel is applied.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The transmitted word is textually uncertain and may reflect a corruption of another anatomical term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A woman characterized by persistent or insatiable sexual appetite.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term describes repeated, closely successive sexual desire or intercourse.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Uninterrupted or closely consecutive in its parts.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Unlike مُتَوَاتِرٌ, it denotes succession without the small intervals associated with the latter term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The name of a prosodic pattern and of the sixteenth classical Arabic poetic metre.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The technical term is associated with specified arrangements of moving and quiescent letters and with the metre built on فَاعِلُنْ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A supplement or addendum supplied to complete an earlier work or statement.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used especially for material added to remedy an omission.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Superfluous or redundant.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported usage in some lexicographical and related works.

cautions: The Quranic endpoint or exhaustion sense of أَدْرَكَ is based on Lane’s discussion of a Quranic reading; no unsupplied modern Quran location is used as an example.
The expression concerning knowledge in the Hereafter under تَدَارَكَ has variant readings and several recorded interpretations.
One Lane unit concerning مَدْرَكٌ is retained as ambiguous because its printed headword may be a mistranscription of مُدْرِكٌ or مُدْرَكٌ.
unassigned_or_ambiguous_evidence: lane-unit:drk:595:g1:sub2: the expression لَهُ مَدْرَكٌ is materially lexical but cannot be assigned confidently because Lane explicitly questions the headword and suggests alternative mistranscriptions.
